translationRepairs: Your minister has heard that when royal affairs fail, then spirits and gods resent resentfully; wickedness and evil disorder the upright—therefore yin and yang are wrong and tangled—this is Heaven's reason for reprimanding and warning the king; it desires to make the lord who has lost the Way suddenly awaken, and make wicked ministers fearful and self-scrutinizing.

Your minister has heard that when royal affairs fail, then spirits and gods grow resentful; wickedness and evil disorder the upright—therefore yin and yang are wrong and tangled—this is Heaven's reason for reprimanding and warning the king; it desires to make the lord who has lost the Way suddenly awaken, and make wicked ministers fearful and self-scrutinizing.

神祇怨怨 is an intensive doubling of one verb of divine resentment, not two English verbs; 'resent resentfully' is ungrammatical, and 'grow resentful' restores a single natural verb without adding meaning.
Yong doubted the impostor; Zhao Xing rode out anyway until Yong slashed the carriage harness with his sword; days later Wang Mang's warrant proved Yong right and made his name.
Yong doubted the impostor; Zhao Xing rode out anyway until Yong slashed the horse's breast-strap with his sword; days later Wang Mang's warrant proved Yong right and made his name.
截馬當匈 names the horse's breast-band (當匈/當胸), not the carriage harness as a whole; the proposed phrase matches the Chinese and the unit's own literal.
He gathered the people for the archery ceremony and invited Peng Feng to watch—planning to seize him there.
He gathered the people for the archery ceremony and invited Feng and the others to watch—planning to seize them there.
請豐等 and 禽之 refer to Feng and his associates, not Peng Feng alone; the original singular omits 等.
Yong saw through it, slew Peng Feng in hand combat, and broke up the band.
Yong saw through it, slew Feng and the others in hand combat, and broke up the band.
手格殺豐等 states that Yong killed Feng and the others, not Peng Feng alone; 禽破黨與 then covers the remaining partisans.
West of the capital he slaughtered an ox on Governor Gou Jian's grave.
He went west to Fufeng and slaughtered an ox on Gou Jian's grave.
西至扶風 is travel west to Fufeng, and 茍諫冢 does not name an office; the original invents 'Governor' and 'the capital,' while the proposal still drops 扶風.
When Grand Minister Han Xin fell foul of the court Yong pleaded for him in vain and offended Guangwu, who sent him out as chancellor of Donghai.
When Grand Minister of Education Han Xin fell foul of the court Yong pleaded for him in vain and offended Guangwu, who sent him out as chancellor of Donghai.
大司徒 is the full Three-Excellencies title Grand Minister of Education; 'Grand Minister' truncates the office named in the Chinese and in this unit's literal.
In year 4 he succeeded Mou Rong as grand commandant; he died in year 6 in his seventies.
In the fourth year of Jianchu he succeeded Mou Rong as grand commandant; he died in the sixth year in his seventies.
四年 and 六年 are bare regnal years of the era already in force for this career close; English 'year 4' and 'year 6' omit that dating, and inserting Jianchu on the first year is the standard completion.
His grandson Bao Ang, courtesy name Shuya, was famed for filial duty and integrity.
His son Bao Ang, courtesy name Shuya, was famed for filial duty and integrity.
子昂 immediately follows De's death in office and means De's son Ang; 'grandson' invents a generation and wrongly points the kinship at Yong.

Yun did not pay court visit—said: 'Formerly King Wen pulled Lü Shang from Wei's bank—Gaozong ritually Fu Yue from cliff building—Duke Huan took Guan Zhong from shooting hook—therefore able to establish vast merit—complete primal merit.

Yun did not pay a court visit, and said: 'Formerly King Wen drew Lü Shang from the Wei bank; Gaozong ritually honored Fu Yue from cliff-building; Duke Huan took Guan Zhong after the hook-shot; therefore they could establish vast merit and complete supreme achievement.
禮傅說 needs an English verb of ritual honor; the original 'Gaozong ritually Fu Yue' is ungrammatical, and the rest of the replacement keeps the three 於-phrases and the concluding merit.
Yun thereupon swore masses, saying: 'Do not ambush others unprepared—drive others to straits—must not sever people's limbs—strip people's skeletons—release wanton women.'
Yun thereupon swore the troops, saying: 'Do not ambush others unprepared, drive others into straits, sever people's limbs, strip people's corpses, or debauch women.'
放淫婦女 prohibits debauching women, not releasing wanton women; 誓眾 in this army setting is an oath to the troops, and 裸人形骸 is stripping corpses.
Yun said: "You do not fear death—you ache that your father is unavenged.
Yun said: "I know you do not grieve Heaven's mandate—you ache that vengeance is unfulfilled.
吾知子不悲天命，而痛仇不復也 opens with 'I know you do not grieve Heaven's mandate' and unnamed unfulfilled vengeance; the original drops 吾知, replaces 天命 with fearing death, and invents 'your father.'
Guangwu told his escort to show themselves in the gate light.
The emperor ordered his escort to show their faces in the gap of the gate.
帝令從者見面於門間 is the emperor ordering attendants to show their faces in the gate gap; 'Guangwu' and 'gate light' are not in this unit.
He refused the order until sure.
He thereupon would not accept the edict.
遂不受詔 is only the refusal of the edict; 'until sure' is an invented motive not present in the Chinese.
Xian once ordered disciple carried document visit Shou—had request entrustment—Shou immediately sent edict prison.
Xian once ordered a disciple to carry a document to visit Shou with a request for favor—Shou immediately sent him to the imperial prison.
壽即送詔獄 means Shou sent the messenger to the imperial prison; 'edict prison' misreads 詔獄 as a kind of edict and drops the human object.
Dou retaliated with charges about buying public land and demanded execution.
Dou, angry, framed Shou with buying public land and slander, and handed him to the clerks for a death sentence.
憲怒，陷壽以買公田誹謗，下吏當誅 names Shou as the framed victim, includes slander with the public-land charge, and sends him to the clerks for execution; the original omits all three.
He noted that Shou had debated the Xiongnu campaign heatedly and sought to buy public land—hardly crimes worthy of prison.

He noted that Shou, sitting in the secretariat, had debated striking the Xiongnu with the other masters of writing, that his arguments were judged excessive, and that after a memorial seeking to buy public land he was bound in prison and impeached for great disrespect.
臣伏見 reports debate 言議過差, a request to buy public land, then 系獄考劾大不敬; 'hardly crimes worthy of prison' invents He Chang's later plea and erases the great-disrespect impeachment stated here.
I brave your wrath and risk annihilation to speak though death closes my eyes—not for Zhi Shou's sake alone.
I brave your wrath and risk annihilation to speak though death closes my eyes—not for Zhi Shou's sake.

非為壽也 denies that the memorial is for Shou; 'alone' invents a residual private motive. The proposal is right to drop that qualifier but weakens 觸死瞽言; keep the original death-and-blind-speech phrasing and only remove 'alone.'
